commands_used: answer 1. I am Tarin, a thief freed from the Owing barge by Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa. She serves the Toh-Reel-Ka, the Secret Warriors of the Xeech-Leel. The Hists along the river are sickening, including Jal-Veesa Hist, and the cause is unknown. 2. Ask Vosh-Leera for her second task, in her house in Jal-Veesa (she is the quest marker). 3. I can talk to her at once, or go through the door to her house. I see no other choice yet. I could also question Weeltul on sap, scar, eggs and Umbriel. 4. I do not know why the trees sicken or what Umbriel did beyond the 4E 48 story. I could find out by asking Vosh-Leera and Weeltul.

answer 1. Vosh-Leera gave me a cup of Jal-Veesa sap, drawn before the scar closed. Trees are joined at the root, so drinking it lets me ask where the sickness is. 2. Drink the sap here in front of Vosh-Leera, then tell her everything I see. 3. Drink it, or refuse/ask Weeltul first about sap. I mean to drink it and report truthfully. 4. I do not know what the sap will do to me or whether it is safe; my Hist blessing resists poison. I could ask Weeltul about sap.

answer 1. I drank the sap and saw a vision: a young grey Hist among pale stilt huts, a woven weir across a creek, and west of the weir on a reed bank a reed hide beside a lone dead tree with clay jars stacked in its shade. This should show where the sickness is. 2. Tell Vosh-Leera everything I saw, here at Jal-Veesa. 3. Tell her all of it truthfully, or leave details out; I will tell the whole truth. 4. I do not know which place the vision shows, who the hide belongs to, or what the jars hold. Vosh-Leera or Weeltul may know.

answer 1. Vosh-Leera recognised my vision as Teel-Fen Weir, a Sedge-Wardens camp south of Jal-Veesa where a young Hist grew from the roots of Jal-Veesa Hist. Jars by a hide suggest someone is keeping sap. 2. Go to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa, the tree-minder on the platform round the tree. 3. Go straight there and talk to Heem-Jasa first, as Vosh-Leera advised, and be careful at the hide. I could also ask Weeltul first. 4. I do not know who keeps the hide and jars, or why, or who the Sedge-Wardens are beyond being weir-wardens. Heem-Jasa may tell me.

answer 1. Heem-Jasa's young Hist was drained of sap and its scar sealed with grey paste three nights ago, not by her people. Strangers, three Unbound Sap-Takers, keep jars at the reed hide west of the weir. They seem to be draining Hists, which may be why the trees sicken. 2. Take the note from the reed hide west of Teel-Fen Weir. 3. Fight the three Sap-Takers, shoot them from the reeds east of the hide, or creep round to the hide's open west side where the jars are stacked and take the note unseen. I prefer sneaking. 4. I do not know who the Unbound Sap-Takers answer to, what the grey paste is, or what the note says. Reading the note and examining the scar and jars may tell me.

answer 1. The Sap-Takers are working for a master who orders them to bring their jars of sap to Karsh-Naal Camp and seal every scar behind them. So someone is draining Hists and sealing them; that is likely why the trees sicken. 2. Return to Heem-Jasa on the platform at Teel-Fen Weir. She will ask whether her tree will live. 3. Tell her the truth, which brings teaching and trade, or ease her with a kind word, which loses her trust. I will be straight with her (truth). 4. I do not know who the crew's master is, where Karsh-Naal Camp is, or whether the tree will live. Heem-Jasa or Vosh-Leera may know.

answer 1. Sap-Takers are draining young and old Hists and sealing the scars, sending jars to Karsh-Naal Camp. This is probably why the trees sicken. I told Heem-Jasa the truth and she will now teach me alchemy and sell me sap, fungus and eggshells. 2. Go to Karsh-Naal Camp, the Naga camp in the marsh east of Teel-Fen Weir, where the jars are taken. 3. Go there directly, or first learn alchemy and buy supplies from Heem-Jasa, or consult Vosh-Leera. 4. I do not know who the master is, why they want the sap, or what the grey paste is. Karsh-Naal Camp may answer.

answer I am Tarin, freed thief working for Vosh-Leera of Jal-Veesa (for the Toh-Reel-Ka). I drank Jal-Veesa sap and saw Teel-Fen Weir, south of town. Heem-Jasa minds its young Hist, whose scar was drained and sealed with grey paste three nights ago. Three Unbound Sap-Takers keep a reed hide west of the weir; I took their note, which orders jars brought to Karsh-Naal Camp and every scar sealed. That is likely why the Hists sicken. I told Heem-Jasa honestly her tree may die; she will now teach me alchemy and sell sap, fungus and eggshells. I carry the note, the Hist blessing (poison resist) and a lockpick, with 0 gold. I did not fight the Sap-Takers, who are still at the hide. Next: go to Karsh-Naal Camp, a Naga camp in the marsh east of the weir. Still unknown: who the master is, why they want the sap, what the grey paste is, and what Umbriel did; Heem-Jasa and Weeltul have Umbriel topics I have not tried.
